findings.where: Where we're starting: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok) and their 'Best hostels ›' lines, on phone and desktop
findings.fault: The cards look like links: each is a white card with a shadow and a hover rule, and has a link-coloured 'Best hostels' line with a chevron. The parts map shows that none of them is a link (p8–p10 are static). Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of this page's three jobs, and on the page that job does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning their next stop taps 'Canggu · Best hostels', nothing happens, and the visit ends there. The 'Explore destinations' button only scrolls down to these dead cards.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank'; footer 'Privacy', 'Terms', 'How we rank' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: Every one of these links points back to this same page, so they are dead. 'How we rank' is the link that backs the hero's 'merit alone' claim, and Privacy and Terms are what a visitor checks before handing over an email address.
findings.who_objects: A wary traveller wants to see the ranking method or the privacy terms before signing up and gets bounced back to the top of the homepage. Some will decide the 'merit alone' claim has nothing behind it.

findings.where: Hero: the coral primary action 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news'
findings.fault: The only way to sign up for launch news is a mailto link. The visitor has to open a mail app, write an email with no subject or prompt, and send it. On phones with no mail app set up, the link does nothing. The label is also a full email address, which wraps to two lines on a phone, so the button reads as an address rather than an action.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on their phone in the middle of a trip wants to tap once to hear about the launch. Most will not write an email to a stranger, so the page collects few contacts.

findings.where: Destination cards: the region labels (BALI, LOMBOK) and the place names (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok)
findings.fault: These are set in a monospace typewriter face, which looks like a font fallback or debug output. The rest of the site uses Quicksand and Nunito Sans.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand fixes Quicksand for headings and card titles. A visitor sees the cards as unfinished or broken, right at the point the page is trying to look ready to launch.

findings.where: Destination cards: the border and the shadow
findings.fault: Each card has a thick purple border, a colour that is not in the palette, and a heavy, wide shadow while at rest. The brand's cards use a thin sand border, and nothing is meant to sit under a heavy shadow at rest.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because purple has no role in the palette and heavy resting shadows are banned. A visitor sees a block that looks borrowed from another site and clashes with the turquoise, sand and ink around it.

findings.where: The 'Where we're starting' heading compared with the hero's MantaHostels heading and its 'The better way to find hostels in Indonesia' line
findings.fault: The section heading is about twice the size of the hero's display type and takes over the bottom of the desktop first screen. If you squint, it is the loudest thing on the page, louder than the product's own message and the coral action.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor's eye goes to a section label instead of what Manta is and what to do, which weakens the hero's message and its one action.

findings.where: Hero: the coral pill button stacked over the 'Explore destinations' outline button
findings.fault: The two buttons have different shapes: a full pill and a square-cornered box with a thin edge. Neither uses the brand's 8px control corner, so the pair looks like it came from two different kits.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the rules file sets an 8px radius for controls. The mismatch makes the hero look less finished.

findings.where: Desktop: the hero text column compared with the nav, the 'Where we're starting' heading and the cards
findings.fault: The hero copy and buttons start about 230px further in than the left edge that the nav wordmark, the section heading and the cards share. The page has no single left edge.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning down the page sees the hero float loose from everything else, so the layout looks unplanned.

findings.fault: 'How we rank' is underlined and 'Destinations' is not, but neither one is the current page, so two nav links get two different treatments for no reason.
findings.who_objects: A visitor may read the underline as 'you are here' or as the only real link. The rules file gives the current page semibold, not an underline.

findings.where: Footer tagline 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali' compared with the Kuta Lombok destination card
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali only, but the page lists Lombok as one of the places Manta is starting.
findings.who_objects: A traveller heading to Lombok cannot tell whether Lombok is covered yet. On a pre-launch site, small contradictions like this cost trust.
